free_tier.stated: Pay As You Go plan with 1,500 data units a month free, then USD 0.01 a unit; a data unit is 1 location x 1 parameter x 1 month; up to 2,500 units per call, historical data from 1940, global forecast models and an air quality forecast; sign-up without credit card.
free_tier.notes: The true unit is a data unit (one location, one parameter, one month of time series, or 1 degree x 1 degree x 1 month for NetCDF), which the unit vocabulary lacks. Ten years of two parameters for ten locations cost 2,400 units. Bulk path: multi-location calls (the Business plan allows 10 locations a call) and JSON, CSV or NetCDF answers; gridded NetCDF is listed under Enterprise. ERA5 history lags by 5 days and recent days are filled from forecasts. Next plan: Business at USD 150 a month with 50,000 units.

per_object_cap.stated: up to 2,500 units per call on Pay As You Go; 5,000 units or 10 locations on Business

retention.stated: not applicable: the unit is a data unit

egress.terms: not applicable: answers are metered in data units

interface_detail: REST over HTTPS at api.oikolab.com (/weather, /archivedforecast, /airquality, /epw, /datasets, /account) with the key in the api-key header; JSON, CSV or NetCDF answers
tooling: any HTTP client; Python and R examples in the docs
chaining: A history-heavy source: decades of hourly ERA5 for many locations in one call; the free units cover 125 location-years of one parameter.

identity_cost.detail: An account is needed for an API key (the key is on the profile page after login); the pricing page says sign-up needs no credit card; the sign-up is a hosted login page that no reader could render, so its fields are unverified.

reliability_note: The most recent 5 days of history are filled from forecasts and overwritten when ERA5 arrives.
confidence_note: Plan and metering are read from the first-party pricing and docs pages; a call with no key answered HTTP 401, so a keyed call was not exercised.
